title: The Date of the 'Cyclopean Wall' at Hebron
author: David Ussishkin (attribution TO VERIFY — see confidenceNotes)
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted journal article. Project stores its own summary of the reassessment's conclusion only; no reproduction of plans, sections, or photographs.
summary: A scholarly reassessment (ZDPV 137 [2021]: 125-136) of Tell Rumeida/Hebron's massive 'cyclopean' perimeter wall, conventionally dated to the Middle Bronze Age and read (e.g. by Ofer, see ofer-1994-hill-country-judah) as reused by Iron I-early Iron II occupants. This article argues instead that both the wall and its abutting glacis were built in the later Iron Age, when Hebron was a fortified city of the kingdom of Judah, not earlier — citing pottery recovered from the rampart make-up that it dates to the 8th-7th centuries BCE. If correct, this wall cannot be cited as evidence for any fortification standing at Hebron in David's era (early Iron IIA, the setting of 2 Samuel 2), directly complicating claim-hebron-town-form's already-cautious 'no wall plan asserted as excavated' framing by suggesting the wall most visible on the tell today is centuries too late rather than merely undated.
